central_topic: Quantifying and correcting the winner's-curse bias of reporting the best searched LLM prompt/pipeline configuration's score on the same benchmark questions used to select it, via searcher-agnostic debiased interval reporting evaluated on synthetic worlds and replayed MMLU-Pro outcomes.
core_methods: empirical-Bayes hierarchical logistic item-response (latent difficulty) posterior-quantile interval
parametric-bootstrap pivot calibration of the EB-IRT interval
naive Wilson interval, Bonferroni and question-resampling reporting baselines
comparators: inference on winners and post-selection inference
efficient multi-prompt evaluation and prompt-format sensitivity
benchmarks: synthetic latent-difficulty worlds (varying N questions, K configs; equal-config null worlds)
architectural_shifts: from per-config binomial/Wilson score to hierarchical latent-difficulty IRT posterior using all logged (question, config, outcome) triples
from 1-D difficulty to config-by-subject interaction (did not beat the simpler variant)
from analytic posterior to parametric-bootstrap pivot calibration (under-covered: 0.77)
result_driven_themes: naive reporting is upward biased (signed bias ~0.037) and under-covers; EB-IRT cuts bias to ~0.014 and interval score from -0.232 to -0.148 at ~0.915 coverage
Bonferroni is valid but wide (-0.196); resampling worst (-0.273)
bootstrap pivot calibration under-covers (0.77) and interaction model did not improve on the simple EB-IRT
selection is ignorable for likelihood under searchers that use only observed outcomes

queries.query: Rasch model item response theory logistic latent ability item difficulty
queries.rationale: Gap method-irt-model-background (high): the Bernoulli(sigma(a_k - b_q)) model behind EB-IRT has no IRT/Rasch lineage cited; this credits the foundations. No IRT or Rasch work is in the current bibliography.

queries.query: hierarchical Bayesian item response model empirical Bayes marginal maximum likelihood Laplace approximation
queries.rationale: Gap method-irt-model-background (high): ties the hierarchical-prior, Laplace-based empirical-Bayes fitting of EB-IRT to prior IRT estimation work. Distinct from the existing Efron empirical-Bayes entries (Tweedie, Stein), which cover shrinkage and selection bias but not IRT fitting.

queries.query: item response theory for language model benchmark evaluation question difficulty
queries.rationale: Gap method-irt-model-background (high): positions EB-IRT against existing IRT-based LLM evaluation. Polo2024EfficientMultiPrompt is already cited, so the query targets IRT-based difficulty modeling beyond it.

queries.query: over-fitting in model selection and subsequent selection bias in performance evaluation
queries.rationale: Gap intro-selection-bias-ml-model-selection (high): supports the introduction's claim that the best candidate's score is biased and its interval ignores selection, from the ML model-selection literature. The current bibliography has only statistical and holdout-reuse work plus Efron1997Bootstrap632 and Recht2019ImageNet.

queries.query: benchmark test set reuse overfitting meta-analysis repeated evaluation machine learning
queries.rationale: Gap intro-selection-bias-ml-model-selection (high): empirical evidence for the size of selection-induced optimism after repeated test-set reuse. Recht2019ImageNet is the only such study cited; this adds breadth without a full literature refresh.

queries.query: large language models as optimizers automatic prompt optimization
queries.rationale: Gap related-work-prompt-optimizers (medium): the claim that no prompt-search work gives selection-aware uncertainty rests on DSPy, MIPRO and Shi2024PromptBAI alone. Adds the main LLM-driven prompt optimizers (e.g. APE, OPRO, ProTeGi lineage) as comparators. Covers the evaluation-overfitting-on-small-validation-sets angle where results allow.
